title: An eventually invertible sequence has stationary telescope legs
statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a triangulated category with countable coproducts [def-weil-triangulated-category, def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $E_0\xrightarrow{u_0}E_1\to\cdots$ be a sequence. Write $S=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}E_r$ with coprojections $\iota_r$, and let $s:S\to S$ satisfy $s\iota_r=\iota_{r+1}u_r$. Choose a distinguished triangle
$$S\xrightarrow{1-s}S\xrightarrow{p}H\longrightarrow S[1],$$
so $H$ is a homotopy colimit and its legs are $\lambda_r=p\iota_r$ [def-kun-truncations]. If some integer $N\ge0$ satisfies that every $u_r$ for $r\ge N$ is an isomorphism, then $\lambda_r:E_r\to H$ is an isomorphism for every $r\ge N$. The assertion holds for every chosen telescope triangle, with its actual legs; there is no compactness or t-structure hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 090Z (definition-derived-colimit), Tag 0CRH (remark-uniqueness-derived-colimit), Tag 0CRJ (lemma-hocolim-subsequence), applied to a tail; constant-tail telescope is the split triangle for 1-successor. This is the eventual-isomorphism consequence, not an ordinary-colimit assertion.

proof.text:
Write $f=1-s$ and $j=\iota_N$. For $i\le k$ write $U_{i,k}:E_i\to E_k$ for the finite transition composite, with $U_{i,i}=1$. Put $a_i=U_{i,N}$ for $i\le N$ and $a_i=U_{N,i}^{-1}$ for $i>N$. Then $a_{i+1}u_i=a_i$ in all cases, including $i=N$. By the coproduct universal property these components give $a:S\to E_N$, with $aj=1$ and $af=0$. Define $l:S\to S$ by its components
$$l\iota_i=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\sum_{k=i}^{N-1}\iota_kU_{i,k}&i<N,\\0&i=N,\\ \displaystyle-\sum_{k=N}^{i-1}\iota_kU_{k,i}^{-1}&i>N.\end{cases}$$
Every sum here is finite and every inverse has indices at least $N$. Thus the formulas define morphisms in the additive category, and the coproduct universal property defines $l$ without any assertion about maps into infinite coproducts.

source.place: Tag 090Z (definition-derived-colimit); explicit finite-sum calculation supplied by Q48, followed by Tags 0146 (lemma-composition-zero) and 0149 (lemma-representable-homological).

proof.text:
On the $i$-th summand, $lf$ is $l\iota_i-l\iota_{i+1}u_i=\iota_i$: for $i<N$ the forward sums cancel except for $k=i$; for $i=N$ use $l\iota_N=0$ and $l\iota_{N+1}=-\iota_Nu_N^{-1}$; for $i>N$ the inverse sums cancel except for $k=i$. Also $fl\iota_i=\iota_i-ja_i$: for $i<N$ expand $f\iota_k=\iota_k-\iota_{k+1}u_k$ and telescope; for $i=N$ both sides are zero; for $i>N$ the negative inverse sum telescopes to $\iota_i-\iota_NU_{N,i}^{-1}$. Equality on all coprojections therefore gives
$$lf=1_S,\qquad fl=1_S-ja.$$

source.place: Tag 090Z (definition-derived-colimit); explicit finite-sum calculation supplied by Q48, followed by Tags 0146 (lemma-composition-zero) and 0149 (lemma-representable-homological).

proof.text: Let $d:H\to S[1]$ be the last arrow of the chosen triangle. The zero-composite clause of lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact, first on this triangle and then on its rotations, gives $pf=0$ and $f[1]d=0$ (the twice rotated first arrow is $-f[1]$). Since $l[1]f[1]=1$ by the preceding identity and functoriality of shift, $d=l[1]f[1]d=0$. This uses only the actual supplied triangle.

source.place: Tag 090Z (definition-derived-colimit); explicit finite-sum calculation supplied by Q48, followed by Tags 0146 (lemma-composition-zero) and 0149 (lemma-representable-homological).

proof.text: Apply clause (i) of lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact to $af=0$, obtaining $b:H\to E_N$ with $bp=a$. Consequently $bpj=aj=1$. Set $h=1_H-pjb$. Then $hp=p-pja=p(1-ja)=pfl=0$. Clause (ii) of that same cited node gives $h=kd$ for some $k:S[1]\to H$; as $d=0$, $h=0$. Thus $pj=\lambda_N$ and $b$ are mutually inverse. Finally $pf=0$ gives $\lambda_i=\lambda_{i+1}u_i$ for each $i$. Induction gives $\lambda_N=\lambda_rU_{N,r}$ for $r\ge N$. The finite composite $U_{N,r}$ is invertible, so $\lambda_r=\lambda_NU_{N,r}^{-1}$ is an isomorphism, as required.
